title: Yes, Prime Minister
subtitle: Oh, if only you could say the right name, everything would be so much easier.

trails.title: Trail ① The Weight of a Name

content.text: Let's start our conversation with a simple exercise. First, please repeat after me: Dittarsdorf.
After all the days you've spent in Vienna, you should be familiar with the name. Tell me, how do you feel about it?

branch.text: Nothing indeed. Well, you've become numb to it after hearing it so many times, on the street corners, in the cafes, every place you go.
You can't blame them for that. Most at least speak kindly of them, so long as you don't pick up on the venom hiding in their words.
These days, to be an opera singer is more glorious than any noble title; it supersedes them all! The Dittarsdorfs are the true nobles, the ones who can create art through "channeling."

content.text: Seems like it's a word as heavy as lead.

branch.text: Haha, you are making light of it again. But fair enough, you're new here, not as familiar with this name as those who live here, murmuring it in their dreams.

Most of the time, it swirls invisibly through the conversations on the street; other times, it is tangible in the signatures of the exhibits, seen in the performances and the metal badges clinging to collars ... and always in the boys and girls who inherit the Dittarsdorf talents.
And just like that, they are thrust into the role of the outstanding Dittarsdorfs, the lady songbird and the artistic painter.

content.text: In truth, I don't know much at all about these "Dittarsdorf."

branch.text: Oh, of course. Well, then, high time to tell you about them.

Vienna, at present, is a splendid, crumbling house. Whenever the waltz starts playing, the roof trembles along with the music. While the dancing crowd—and funny that it is a crowd—none of them dare look up at it!

The people here live in identical, pretty, little houses, the social classes smoothed out like butter on a cake. Now, works of art become their icons, and in their madness, they scramble to make these beautiful, dazzling things.

The Dittarsdorfs, nobles who can perform channeling, are made to perform like dancing animals in a circus. Businessmen and nobles clamoring to sponsor their performances in order to glorify themselves.
The noble ladies prefer to curate the finest acts, highlighting their good taste and fashionability, while the lordlings seem to prefer new and hidden talents as some example of their virtue.

How, then, could a good singer ever miss a performance? But she must, to take her chance, seizing the lovely bird in her hand—that poor, noble little bird, because people said that she was born with madness.
And it is in this act of "fighting against her madness" that she proves herself proper among the noble ladies.
She knows better than anyone why a piece of art is valuable, and how to make it worth even more.

items.text: Yes, Prime Minister
Outside the temple of art, the mentor imparts a final set of admonitions to her apprentice.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Remember, Marcus, the working staff of the Foundation branch will take care of the dispute in their fashion. We just need to follow him in.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The members of "The Circle" are top priority, but before any of them can be convicted, as said before, all we have to do is ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... Silently observe and respect their lives.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Understood.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I almost bumped into her! That lady in green seemed to be in a bad mood.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Shall I ask the gentleman from the branch who she is? Hmm, he seems busy at the moment ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But that gentleman is a person of this era. If I interrupt him, am I also interrupting his original course of action?
Marcus sinks back into her mire of indecision.
Hofmann gently pats Marcus's shoulder, drawing back her focus.
Fortunately, the Vienna branch's officer does not notice this minor episode.
His attention is captured by the arrival of an uninvited acquaintance.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: My, my, Mr. Rigoletto! Your hair has grown so fast ... To what do we owe the pleasure? Are you also here for the exquisite art?

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Can you just be normal for once, Heinrich? And stop calling me by those opera names!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Someone reported an arcane disturbance here. I see candles ... Are you holding a seance?

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: I must remind you that arcane rituals are not allowed unless you have a separate permit!

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: Excuse me? That's not fair! The first permit already costed us a ...

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Please calm yourself, sir, and be mindful of what you implied. The Viennese government has ensured you the greatest possible freedom through working with us.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Who do you think cleaned up after you people after those fires, passionate murders, and deadly stampedes? We can't bear the consequences of your "moments of epiphany" forever!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Not to mention the seance is one of the most dangerous acts. We've had two colleagues injured, still being treated for mental illness in the Vienna General Hospital.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: You will find no other place as tolerant and open-minded as this one. In return, you should do your part and cooperate with the government.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Seance? What seance? Nothing of the sort, Mr. Rigoletto. This is just a ... rehearsal of the play.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The candles, the settings, and of course, these paintings once bathed in fire!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Yes, this is an art exhibit, a youth rally, or as we prefer to call it, a visualization of the future.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: I demand a rational conversation. Now, I must question the sanity of this gathering—is there no one here who is of sound mind?

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: If not, I'll have to ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I am terribly sorry ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Mr. Strauss, sorry to have kept you waiting.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Ms. Dittarsdorf!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Bless you, Madam. I did not expect to see you here!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Oh, sorry that we've troubled you. I'm here for my late brother's exhibition, and for a rehearsal of the coming performance.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: We, we got a little carried away! Made you come all the way here to check on us ...

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Please, madam. As your friend, I do not wish to cause you discomfort. In fact, Mr. Karl and I were talking about you over brunch earlier, he was truly impressed by your talent at the opera!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ah, Mr. Karl is too kind. Since my mother passed away, he has been such a caring friend to the family.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Well then, this was all just a misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: But madam, please understand that I still have procedures to go through.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Ahem, would you mind if I ... investigated a little?
The man leans in, his voice a hushed whisper.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: By "investigate," you know ... just a quick look around the building.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: We are grateful to have a responsible employee like you, Mr. Strauss. Please, help yourself.
At the other end of the hall, investigators from headquarters uphold their duties with familiar diligence and effort.
Hofmann imperceptibly shakes her coat, as fine threads, like spider silk, disperse into the air attached to tiny floating particles.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Wow, the "Spider Tail" and the "Detection Spores" ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: These are Laplace's auxiliary devices for perceiving arcane power ... I've never seen one before. Only investigators of level four or higher are allowed to use them ...
Noticing the excited glances towards her, Hofmann leans in to whisper to the young investigator.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, come, give me a hand.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: On it.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: These burnt pictures ... they're the work of Theophil von Dittarsdorf.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: They're the perfect subjects for "reading."
The lamp is gripped a little tighter. She lifts her head, as she begins "reading," the world around her becomes a matter of effortless ease to view.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Only a third of the picture can be "read" ... But I can see it clearly.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mmm! An ingenious composition that balances the different elements of the picture. Sadly, the creator focused too much on the form and overlooked the content. The frame is made of ... Ah, not important. Next page.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This one is luckier. Half of it survived the fire, so we can see the lower half of the lady in the picture. But ... eh, Theophil certainly had a way with women. She was not his first prey.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And this one, only a frame remains. The rest of his works are too damaged, but I do remember an intact one somewhere ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... But aside from this, I don't see anything else. Next page.
She turns, colliding with a pair of light-colored eyes.
Despite the distance, it feels as though Isolde is gazing back at her.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: People can be "read" too. That person, Ms. Isolde ...
A deep breath. The page unfolds before her eyes once again.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Unlike other ladies pursuing the latest fashions in Paris, she still wears the corset, with only some Art Nouveau jewelry by her waist. She's as delicate as a butterfly.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: She is a renowned medium. The Dittarsdorf family is well known for their mediumship. Nowadays they use that power mostly for art. That is, they summon a spirit to possess their body so they can sing, write, and paint like no other.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: They also suffered for this power. Wracked by neurosis and hysteria, the family has had very few members despite its long history.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Wait a minute ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That picture behind her is still intact! And ... it is enormous ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It that ... The Salvation?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Strange. This painting is ...?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: You have a keen eye for art, Miss.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah!
A voice leaps up behind her, bursting from behind the warm smile of the freckle-faced man.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: This painting is the work of my dearest friend, Siegmund—The Salvation! The only piece he left behind that survived the consuming flames.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: These enchanting, magical circles, one next to another ... Oh, I was only reciting Ms. Kakania. We're both passionate about the subject.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: How regrettable, she would've given you a much better explanation if she were here. Her words can easily stir one's soul.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Did you say Kakania? You have a friend called Kakania?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Oh, yes. Every artist has their own nickname. I also have the honor of knowing the Orange Knight, Victor of the Rhine, Apfelstrudel ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Are you a friend of Kakania? Too bad she just left. She should be meeting with Dr. Schwartz by now.
Marcus looks up. Her mentor casts her eyes to the same spot and shakes her head gently.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, the name sounded a little strange to me, that's all ... But I appreciate the explanation, sir.
In the air, the dispersed spores stir imperceptibly.
*bang! bang! crash!*
The dust from the explosion pervades the air, sucking deep into nostrils and open mouths.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: *cough* What happened?!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Are these ... ghosts? Didn't you say there wasn't a seance? Ms. Dittarsdorf, I would very much like an explanation.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Whoa! They're still chasing me.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... The "Detection Spores" have taken effect and enveloped the ghosts. Marcus, can you still "read"?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm ... I think so!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Good. I'll draw its attention. You take care of the arcanum part.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Ms. Dittarsdorf, you told me this was just an opera rehearsal. Now look at this mess—and more importantly, my two assistants are still here!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: I must ask you for a good reason to report to my superior.
The pale girl remains silent, bowing her head.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh! Isolde, my dear, lovely girl.
An all-too-familiar mustachioed face arrives without invitation.
Karl's steps are at a steady trouncing waddle as he approaches and takes Isolde's hand.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Mr. Karl!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Director.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Look at you, so pale! The play is sapping your strength. Come, child, come to me.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I told Schwartz to take good care of you! Well, I guess he can't be in two places at once. The frequent presentations must've been too much for a doctor such as he.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I've learned that you've recovered from hysteria, which is good, but promise me that you'll look after yourself, will you? Your late mother suffered a tragic end, and it'd be unbearable for the Empire to lose another star.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You flatter me.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Joseph.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Yes, director.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Don't be so hard on them, those were wonderful stage effects! Heinrich is an expert at this, yes? What better demonstrates our free will than respecting the artists and their work?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: None of us would mind an episode of excitement every once in a while!
Karl meets Hofmann's eyes in another overly affable attempt at good nature.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Even the gentlemen from the headquarters would agree with me, don't you think?

items.speaker: Foundation Staff
items.text: Yes, you're right ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: We are short on manpower, and the assistants should focus on more important matters.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Hm. We should leave.
TO BE CONTINUED…
